title: How Plant Parts Work
keyIdea: Each plant part has a job: roots take in water and minerals, the stem carries them up, leaves make food with light, and flowers help make seeds.
familyTip: Point to a houseplant: 'Where does water go in? Where is food made? Where might seeds form?' Cover one leaf for a few days and compare colour.

visual.caption: Match each plant part to its job. Drag, or tap a card then a box.

items: hold the plant in the soil

lab.caption: Flagship lab: show roots absorbing, stem transport, leaves making food, flowers making seeds, then predict failure.

kid: Roots grow under the soil. They take in water and minerals. They do not eat the soil.
The stem holds the plant up. It is also a path that carries water up to the leaves.
Leaves use light, air and water to make the plant’s food. That is why leaves need light.
Flowers help the plant make seeds. Seeds can grow into new plants.
adult: Year 3 plants: roots take in water and minerals and hold the plant. The stem holds it up and carries water. Leaves make food with light. Flowers help make seeds. Words: absorb, transport, light-food, seeds.
Common mistakes: thinking plants eat soil; saying leaves are just pretty; thinking the stem only holds the plant up; treating flowers as only decoration.
In the lab your child shows water going in at the roots and up the stem, lets leaves make food, makes seeds at the flower, and predicts wilting when roots fail.

practice.hint: Think about what enters the plant underground.
practice.explain: Roots absorb water and minerals from the soil; they do not eat soil.

practice.hint: Food-making needs light on the green parts.
practice.explain: Leaves make food by photosynthesis using light, air and water.

practice.prompt: A plant has {n} leaves making food. How many leaf jobs is that?
practice.hint: Each leaf still does the same food-making job.
practice.explain: All {n} leaves share the food-making job; the count of leaves is {=n}.

practice.prompt: Water rises through {n} stem sections. How many transport paths is that?
practice.hint: Count the stem sections that carry water upward.
practice.explain: The stem’s job is transport; {n} sections still mean {=n} path pieces in this model.

practice.prompt: Order: water’s path in a healthy plant.
items: leaves use water to make food
practice.hint: Start underground, then move upward to the leaves.
practice.explain: Absorption at roots, transport in the stem, then use in leaves.

pool.prompt: The stem’s main job is to…
pool.hint: Think of the stem as a pathway, not a mouth.
pool.explain: The stem supports the plant and transports water and minerals upward.

pool.hint: Link flowers to new plants and seeds.
pool.explain: Flowers enable reproduction so the plant can produce seeds.
If roots fail, water and minerals cannot be absorbed, so the plant wilts.
Leaves make food using light; roots take in water and minerals, not food.

pool.prompt: Cover {n} leaves. How many covered leaves make less food?
pool.hint: Covered leaves cannot use light well.
pool.explain: Each covered leaf makes less food; covering {n} leaves affects {=n} leaves.

pool.prompt: A plant makes {n} seeds. How many new-plant starts is that?
pool.hint: Each seed can start a new plant.
pool.explain: {n} seeds means {=n} potential new plants from reproduction.
Roots absorb water and minerals from the soil.

pool.prompt: Order: jobs from soil to seed.
pool.hint: Start with intake, then carry, then reproduction.
pool.explain: Absorb, transport, then reproduction at the flower.
